prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Disclosed are a communication technique for merging, with IoT technology, a 5G communication system for supporting a data transmission rate higher than that of a 4G system, and a system therefor. The disclosed technique and system can be applied to intelligent services (for example, smart home, smart building, smart city, smart car or connected car, health care, digital education, retailing, security and safety related services, and the like) on the basis of 5G communication technology and IoT related technology. A method for controlling uplink transmission power of a terminal in a wireless communication system comprises the steps of: initializing a power control adjustment value when a repetition level for a coverage enhancement mode is changed; updating the power control adjustment value according to a transmission power control (TPC) command received from a base station; calculating uplink transmission power on the basis of the updated power control adjustment value and the repetition level; and transmitting uplink data or control information by the calculated uplink transmission power.

Disclosed are a communication technique and corresponding system for integrating, with Internet of Things (IoT) technology, a 5G communication system that supports a data transmission rate higher than that of a 4G system. The disclosed technique and system may be applied to intelligent services, such as smart homes, smart buildings, smart cities, smart cars or connected cars, healthcare, digital education, retail, security and safety-related services, and the like, based on 5G communication technology and IoT-related technology.

A method for controlling uplink transmission power of a terminal in a wireless communication system includes: initializing a power control adjustment value when a repetition level for a coverage enhancement mode is changed; updating the power control adjustment value according to a transmission power control (TPC) command received from a base station; calculating uplink transmission power based on the updated power control adjustment value and the repetition level; and transmitting uplink data or control information using the calculated uplink transmission power.
outputs.L2:
A communication method and corresponding system are presented for integrating IoT technology with a 5G communication system that supports data transmission speeds exceeding those of 4G systems. The method and system may be used for intelligent services based on 5G communication technology and IoT-related technology, including, for example, smart homes, smart buildings, smart cities, smart cars or connected vehicles, healthcare, digital education, retail, security, safety-related services, and similar applications.

A method for managing uplink transmit power of a terminal in a wireless communication system includes: resetting a power control adjustment value when a repetition level associated with a coverage enhancement mode changes; modifying the power control adjustment value in accordance with a transmission power control, TPC, command received from a base station; determining uplink transmit power using the modified power control adjustment value and the repetition level; and sending uplink data or control information using the determined uplink transmit power.
outputs.L3:
The disclosed technique relates to a wireless communication method that combines 5G communication technology with Internet of Things (IoT) technology. By integrating these technologies, the technique supports data transmission rates higher than those provided by conventional 4G systems and enables more efficient communication in advanced network environments.

This technique may be applied to a wide range of intelligent services. Examples include smart home services, smart city infrastructure, connected vehicles, healthcare services, digital education, retail platforms, and security-related services. In these applications, reliable and efficient wireless communication is important for supporting large numbers of connected devices, real-time data exchange, and improved service quality.

More specifically, the technique provides a method for controlling uplink transmission power of a terminal in a wireless communication system. Uplink transmission power control is important because it helps maintain reliable communication between the terminal and the base station while reducing unnecessary power consumption and limiting interference with other devices.

In the proposed method, the terminal operates in a coverage enhancement mode in which repeated transmission may be used to improve communication reliability. When the repetition level associated with the coverage enhancement mode changes, the terminal initializes a power control adjustment value. This initialization allows the terminal to reset or reconfigure its power control state in response to the changed repetition level, thereby helping to maintain proper uplink power control under the new transmission conditions.

After the initialization, the terminal receives a transmit power control (TPC) command from the base station. The terminal updates the power control adjustment value based on the received TPC command. The updated adjustment value is then used, together with the repetition level, to calculate the uplink transmission power. Using the calculated transmission power, the terminal transmits uplink data or uplink control information to the base station.

Through this process, the technique enables more accurate uplink power control when coverage enhancement settings change. As a result, the terminal can maintain reliable uplink communication, reduce power waste, and support efficient operation in 5G and IoT-based wireless communication systems.
outputs.L4:
A 5G-IoT wireless communication method is provided for controlling uplink transmission power of a terminal operating in an enhanced-coverage environment. In such an environment, the terminal may transmit the same uplink data or control information repeatedly according to a coverage-enhancement repetition level, so that a base station can reliably receive the transmission even when radio conditions are poor. Because the required uplink power may vary depending on the repetition level, the method manages a power control adjustment value in association with changes in the repetition level and with transmit power control information received from the base station.

According to the method, the terminal first determines whether a coverage-enhancement repetition level has changed. The repetition level may indicate the number of times an uplink signal, an uplink data channel, or an uplink control channel is repeatedly transmitted to improve reception reliability. When the repetition level changes, the terminal initializes a power control adjustment value. This initialization prevents an adjustment value accumulated under a previous repetition level from being incorrectly applied to a new repetition level, thereby reducing the risk of excessive or insufficient uplink transmission power.

After the initialization, the terminal receives a transmit power control command from a base station. The transmit power control command may be included in downlink control information or another control signaling message transmitted by the base station. Based on the received command, the terminal updates the initialized power control adjustment value. For example, the command may instruct the terminal to increase, decrease, or maintain its uplink transmission power. The terminal applies the command to the power control adjustment value so that the value reflects both the current radio link condition and the current coverage-enhancement operation.

The terminal then calculates uplink transmission power using the updated power control adjustment value and the current coverage-enhancement repetition level. The calculated transmission power may further take into account parameters such as a configured maximum transmission power, path loss, target received power, resource allocation information, modulation and coding scheme, bandwidth, or other power control parameters defined for the 5G-IoT system. By incorporating the repetition level into the calculation, the terminal can determine a transmission power that is suitable for repeated transmission in enhanced coverage, rather than merely reusing a power level intended for ordinary coverage or for a different repetition level.

The calculated uplink transmission power is used by the terminal to transmit uplink data, uplink control information, random access signaling, or other IoT-related traffic to the base station. As a result, the base station can receive the transmitted information with improved reliability while unnecessary power consumption and interference may be reduced. This is particularly useful for IoT terminals, which often operate with limited battery capacity and may be installed in locations having poor radio coverage, such as basements, factories, underground facilities, vehicles, remote sensors, or indoor smart devices.

By initializing the power control adjustment value when the coverage-enhancement repetition level changes and then updating the value according to a base-station transmit power control command, the method enables more accurate and stable uplink power control. It avoids inappropriate accumulation of power control offsets across different repetition levels and helps ensure that the terminal uses an uplink power level suited to the current enhanced-coverage state.

This wireless communication method can therefore support reliable transmission of data and control signals in 5G-IoT networks. It may be applied to a wide range of intelligent IoT services, including smart home systems, smart city infrastructure, connected vehicles, industrial automation, healthcare monitoring, public safety systems, environmental sensing, logistics tracking, and security services. Through improved uplink power control in enhanced-coverage scenarios, the method contributes to efficient network operation, longer terminal battery life, reduced interference, and more dependable IoT connectivity.
outputs.L5:
**The Future of IoT: Disclosed Opportunities and Challenges**

The rapid growth of the Internet of Things, or IoT, is transforming the way people live, work, and interact with technology. IoT refers to the network of connected devices that collect, exchange, and analyze data through the internet. From smart homes and wearable devices to industrial sensors and connected vehicles, IoT is becoming an important part of modern life.

As more IoT technologies are developed, many new opportunities are being disclosed to businesses, governments, and consumers. Companies can use IoT systems to improve efficiency, reduce costs, and make better decisions based on real-time data. For example, smart factories can monitor machines to prevent breakdowns, while smart cities can use connected systems to manage traffic, energy use, and public safety.

However, the expansion of IoT also creates important challenges. The more devices that are connected, the greater the risk of cyberattacks, data breaches, and privacy concerns. Sensitive information may be collected and shared, making it essential for companies to protect user data and clearly explain how it is used. Security standards, encryption, and responsible data management are necessary to build trust in IoT solutions.

The future of IoT depends on balancing innovation with safety and transparency. As new technologies are disclosed and adopted, organizations must focus not only on performance but also on privacy, security, and ethical use. If managed responsibly, IoT has the potential to create smarter, safer, and more efficient communities around the world.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for a 5G/IoT wireless communication invention about controlling uplink transmission power when the coverage enhancement repetition level changes.
counterfactuals.output: A method, apparatus, and computer-readable medium are disclosed for controlling uplink transmission power in a wireless communication system supporting coverage enhancement for Internet of Things (IoT) devices. A user equipment determines a change in a coverage enhancement repetition level associated with uplink transmission, wherein the repetition level defines a number of repetitions for transmitting an uplink signal or channel. In response to the change, the user equipment updates one or more uplink power control parameters, including at least one of a target received power, path loss compensation factor, maximum transmit power, power ramping value, or closed-loop power control adjustment. The updated transmission power is applied to a subsequent uplink transmission, such as a random access preamble, physical uplink shared channel, or control channel, based on the new repetition level. By coordinating power control with repetition-level transitions, the disclosed technique reduces excessive transmit power, improves coverage reliability, limits interference to neighboring cells, and enhances battery efficiency for 5G and IoT wireless devices operating under varying radio coverage conditions.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a Korean patent application summary in English for a method where a terminal initializes a power control adjustment value upon repetition level changes and updates it using TPC commands from a base station.
counterfactuals.output: A terminal receives configuration information for uplink transmission from a base station, including a repetition level indicating the number of repeated transmissions. The terminal maintains a power control adjustment value used for determining uplink transmission power. When the repetition level is changed, the terminal initializes the power control adjustment value, for example by resetting the accumulated adjustment value to an initial value. Thereafter, the terminal receives transmit power control (TPC) commands from the base station and updates the initialized power control adjustment value according to the received TPC commands. The terminal determines uplink transmission power based on the updated power control adjustment value and transmits an uplink signal using the determined power. Accordingly, uplink power control can be performed appropriately even when a repetition level is changed, thereby improving transmission reliability and preventing excessive or insufficient transmission power.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract for a telecommunications patent describing uplink power control in a wireless system supporting 5G and IoT intelligent services such as smart home, connected cars, healthcare, and security.
counterfactuals.output: A method, apparatus, and system are disclosed for uplink power control in a wireless communication network supporting fifth generation (5G) and Internet of Things (IoT) intelligent services, including smart home, connected vehicle, healthcare, and security applications. A wireless device determines an uplink transmit power based on one or more service characteristics, channel conditions, traffic priority, latency requirements, device power constraints, and network configuration information received from a base station. The network may configure service-specific power control parameters, including target received power, path loss compensation, power control step size, resource allocation, and maximum transmit power, to balance coverage, reliability, interference mitigation, and energy efficiency. The wireless device adjusts uplink power dynamically for data, control, and reference signal transmissions according to the configured parameters and real-time measurements. The disclosed techniques enable reliable low-latency communication for critical IoT services while reducing interference and conserving battery power for massive IoT devices in heterogeneous 5G wireless systems.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a formal patent disclosure paragraph for a method of calculating UE uplink transmit power based on a transmission power control command and a coverage enhancement mode repetition level.
counterfactuals.output: In one embodiment, a method is provided for determining an uplink transmit power of a user equipment (UE) operating in a wireless communication network. The method comprises receiving, by the UE, a transmission power control (TPC) command from a network node and determining a coverage enhancement mode repetition level associated with an uplink transmission to be performed by the UE. The UE calculates an uplink transmit power based at least in part on the received TPC command and the determined coverage enhancement mode repetition level, wherein the repetition level corresponds to a number of repeated transmissions or a coverage enhancement state configured for the UE. In certain implementations, the UE applies a power adjustment value indicated by the TPC command to a baseline uplink power value and further modifies the baseline uplink power value, the power adjustment value, or both, as a function of the repetition level, such that different repetition levels result in different uplink transmit power calculations. The UE then transmits an uplink signal or channel using the calculated uplink transmit power, thereby enabling power control that accounts for both network-directed power adjustment and coverage enhancement operation.
